audit_findings.title: Current leverage and FY2025 owner earnings carry different interest burdens
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed current annual interest at 5.7% on $400.0 million is approximately $22.8 million, versus filed FY2025 interest expense of $23.249 million and cash interest of $21.991 million; the differences are $0.449 million lower and $0.809 million higher, respectively, both below 0.5% of $174.9 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-level OE retains interest expense; the $150.0 million incremental borrowing also funded repurchases reflected in the current share count
audit_findings.evidence: As of August 30, 2025, the outstanding balance of the Term Facility was $250.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The increase from $250.0 million to $400.0 million of debt is demonstrated, but an omitted material interest burden is not. The current run-rate interest burden is close to the burden already embedded in FY2025 earnings because the effective rate declined. The later filing also shows $150.0 million of borrowing and $213.2 million of repurchases, so the associated share reduction is in the current denominator.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the OE worksheet begins with FY2025 earnings after the full $23.249 million interest expense and rerun only if current contractual interest, fee amortization, or fully diluted shares differ materially from the filed figures.

audit_findings.title: Growth working-capital needs may have been normalized away
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 working-capital cash use of $32.9 million, equal to 18.8% of $174.9 million anchor OE; $51.9 million adverse year-over-year swing; latest thirty-nine-week cash use was $24.4 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring inventory, receivables, or promotion-related investment omitted from the OE anchor or forecasts increases projected OE and its terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in working capital consumed cash of $32.9 million in the fifty-two weeks ended August 30, 2025, compared to $19.0 million of cash provided in the fifty-three weeks ended August 31, 2024, a difference of $51.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash consumption is demonstrated and continued in fiscal 2026, but the record does not show how much is permanent growth investment versus timing. Because the FY2025 use alone is nearly one-fifth of anchor OE, excluding a recurring portion is reasonably capable of materially overstating value, particularly in the 5% and 8% growth cases.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each working-capital component in the FY2025 OE worksheet, estimate the sales-linked recurring requirement using FY2025 and fiscal-2026 data, and rerun every scenario with that requirement deducted.

audit_findings.title: Not all cash added to equity value may be excess or upstreamable
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum disputed bridge amount is $123.884 million, or $1.32 per diluted share and 4.3% of base equity value; removing all of it reduces base value from $30.47 to approximately $29.15 and buy-below from $21.33 to approximately $20.41, still well above the $11.45 price
audit_findings.mechanism: Unavailable or required operating cash would reduce the cash added in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: We currently depend on Atkins Intermediate Holdings, LLC for distributions, loans and other payments to generate the funds necessary to meet our financial obligations and to pay any dividends regarding our common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: Restrictions and minimum operating-cash needs remain unresolved, but even the conservative extreme of removing the entire balance cannot change the stated purchase conclusion. This is therefore not material to the conclusion at the supplied market price, although it affects the reported intrinsic-value estimate.
audit_findings.action: Obtain legal-entity cash balances, covenant restrictions, near-term liquidity requirements, and normalized minimum cash; replace the bridge amount with verified excess cash in the next routine rerun.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 earnings benefited from reduced marketing spend
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 selling-and-marketing expense decreased $9.647 million and advertising costs decreased $26.9 million, from $103.0 million to $76.1 million; fiscal-2026 third-quarter selling and marketing increased $5.374 million year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporarily low recurring marketing expense raises anchor OE and margins while the growth scenarios assume continuing brand support and expansion
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease was primarily related to an overall decrease in marketing spend.
audit_findings.explanation: The expense reduction is demonstrated, while its sustainable amount is unresolved. The subsequent quarterly spending increase and the need to restore OWYN velocity support the possibility that FY2025 was below a maintainable level. The advertising decline equals 15.4% of anchor OE before tax, making normalization reasonably capable of materially reducing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct advertising and total selling-and-marketing expense by brand and year, identify temporary campaign timing, and rerun OE and growth scenarios using the spending required to sustain each brand's assumed sales trajectory.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE growth and RONTA mix organic performance with acquisitions
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed OWYN net consideration was $280.172 million; OE increased $138.2 million from 2017 to 2025, while the computed base-versus-bear valuation spread is $663 million or $7.05 per share; acquisition-adjusted organic OE and full Quest purchase capital are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings can inflate historical growth and RONTA if purchase consideration is excluded, potentially supporting excessive forecast growth rather than entering OE directly
audit_findings.evidence: As part of Simply Good Foods’ strategy to become an industry leading snacking platform, in November 2019, we acquired Quest Nutrition, LLC (“Quest”) and we acquired Only What You Need, Inc. in June 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The inclusion of Quest and OWYN in the historical series is demonstrated; the organic contribution and correct acquisition-inclusive return are not established. Because moving from 0% to 5% growth changes value by $7.05 per share, a growth calibration influenced by acquisition-driven step-ups is reasonably capable of materially changing valuation. The 163.8% RONTA is not reliable evidence of organic reinvestment productivity until acquisition capital is included.
audit_findings.action: Build pro-forma brand-level OE for a consistent ownership perimeter, include the full Quest and OWYN purchase consideration in invested capital, recompute organic growth and RONTA, and rerun the growth cases from those results.

audit_findings.title: Atkins decline may contradict consolidated perpetual growth
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed Atkins North America sales fell $74.469 million, or 22.6%, in the latest thirty-nine weeks; consolidated sales fell 5.4% and adjusted EBITDA fell 20.5%; the computed base-versus-bear valuation spread is $663 million or $7.05 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Persistent Atkins contraction reduces consolidated OE and may invalidate the 5%-8% initial growth paths and the eventual 2.5% terminal growth assumption
audit_findings.evidence: The Atkins brand has had, and continues to have, a large retail presence on-shelf, which is being reduced in fiscal year 2026 and could be reduced in future periods.
audit_findings.explanation: This is no longer solely forward-looking: substantial Atkins sales decline, shelf reductions, consolidated contraction, and lower adjusted EBITDA are demonstrated. Whether Quest and OWYN can offset the decline is unresolved, and OWYN itself showed velocity-related weakness. Since the difference between the base and zero-growth cases is $7.05 per share, the issue is clearly capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Forecast OE separately for Atkins, Quest, and OWYN using current distribution, velocity, gross margin, replacement-product economics, and required marketing; then rerun consolidated bear, base, bull, and terminal-growth assumptions.
